To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) The ionization in two color pulses can be controlled by engineering the temporal shape of the carrier-wave envelope; 2) This effect is driven by local field maxima in the temporal envelope; and 3) The ionization yield can be controlled by the shape of the envelope even in the case of pulses with the same carrier frequency.
the ionization in optical filamentation is driven by local peaks of the electric-field strength and is adiabatically dependent on the carrier-wave envelope.

(i) the ionization yield in a two-color pulse is determined by the local electric-field strength and its temporal derivative; (ii) the carrier-wave shape effects are adiabatic and are not affected by the carrier-envelope phase; (iii) the carrier-wave effects can be exploited to control the filamentation process and to enhance the ionization yield.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interaction of intense ultrashort light pulses with atoms and molecules.
the interaction of intense ultrashort laser pulses with gases.
the interaction of intense laser fields with matter, in particular, the ionization and dissociation of molecules in strong laser fields.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the carrier-envelope phase is not important for the ionization of atoms in a filament.
the carrier-wave shape is a crucial factor that should be accounted for in the modeling of strong field ionization in multicolor optical filaments.
the observed effects are a consequence of a strong-field ionization process, and that the ionization is driven by local peaks of the carrier-envelope phase of the excitation field.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we show that the carrier-wave shape effects in ionization in optical fields is adiabatically driven by the local field peaks, and that the ionization is a local effect.

the ionization yield is enhanced in a filament created by a two-color pulse, and the ionization is localized at the position of the peak intensity in the carrier wave of the pulse, and the peak ionization yield is determined by the peak of the electric field of the carrier wave.

the adiabaticity of the strong field ionization process in optical filaments is a key feature that enables the use of the pulse shape to engineer the ionization yield and the spatial structure of the optical filament.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the carrier-wave shape effects in strong-field ionization are as important as those of the envelope, and should be considered in the modeling of the interaction of intense light fields with matter.
the carrier-envelope phase and sub-cycle carrier-wave shape effects can be used to control the ionization yield and the spatial distribution of the ionization in optical filamentation.
, in order to model the effects of carrier-envelope phase on the ionization dynamics, one has to account for the spatio-temporal structure of the optical field.
